---
title: "Buck-boost converter"
subtitle: "Power electronics"
toc: true
---

The classic (inverting) buck-boost can step the output above *or* below the input, at the cost of an inverted polarity — the output is referenced negative to the input's ground. Same ideal CCM treatment as the buck and boost pages.

## Duty cycle

$$
\frac{|V_{out}|}{V_{in}} = \frac{D}{1-D} \quad \Rightarrow \quad D = \frac{|V_{out}|}{V_{in} + |V_{out}|}
$$

$D < 0.5$ steps down, $D > 0.5$ steps up — the same switch duty cycle range covers both directions, which is the whole appeal of the topology.

## Inductor current

The inductor is charged from $V_{in}$ only, during the on-time — same charging behavior as a boost:

$$
\Delta I_L = \frac{V_{in} D}{f_{sw} L} \quad \Rightarrow \quad L = \frac{V_{in} D}{f_{sw}\, \Delta I_L}
$$

And the output only sees current during the off-time, so — again like a boost —

$$
I_{L,avg} = \frac{I_{out}}{1-D}
$$

This is the least efficient of the three topologies in practice: the inductor carries both the input and output current duty cycles, so RMS current (and core/copper loss) tends to be the highest of the three for a given output power.

## Calculator

```{=html}
<div id="buckboost-calc"></div>
<script src="../assets/js/calc-engine.js"></script>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "buckboost-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "Vin", label: "Vin (V)", value: 12, min: 0.01, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "Vout", label: "|Vout| (V)", value: 12, min: 0.01, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "fsw", label: "fsw (kHz)", value: 500, min: 1, step: 10 },
    { id: "Iout", label: "Iout (A)", value: 1, min: 0.001, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "ripplePct", label: "Ripple (% of IL,avg)", value: 30, min: 1, step: 1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "D", label: "Duty cycle D" },
    { id: "ILavg", label: "IL,avg" },
    { id: "dIL", label: "ΔIL" },
    { id: "L", label: "L required" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    if (v.Vin <= 0 || v.Vout < 0) return { D: "invalid", ILavg: "-", dIL: "-", L: "-" };
    var D = v.Vout / (v.Vin + v.Vout);
    var fsw = v.fsw * 1000;
    var ILavg = v.Iout / (1 - D);
    var dIL = (v.ripplePct / 100) * ILavg;
    var L = dIL > 0 ? (v.Vin * D) / (fsw * dIL) : 0;
    return {
      D: D.toFixed(3),
      ILavg: ILavg.toFixed(3) + " A",
      dIL: dIL.toFixed(3) + " A",
      L: (L * 1e6).toFixed(2) + " µH"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
